method: OPEN AND QUOTED from DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC) 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)' (published 21 June 2026). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13432566).

claims.claim: **Weight symptom burden equally with blood counts and clinical findings.** Measure it with the MPN-SAF TSS, which scores 10 core symptoms.
claims.source_text: Consequently, the guidelines now elevate symptoms to an equivalent status alongside clinical and hematological parameters. … This tool captures 10 core MF‐associated symptoms-including fatigue, night sweats, bone pain, pruritus, anorexia, weight loss, and splenomegaly‐related discomfort-by grading their frequency and severity on a numerical scale.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Score symptoms at every visit.** A fall of ≥ 50% in the MPN-SAF TSS counts as a clinically meaningful response. Symptom progression on its own, without haematological progression, is enough to escalate or change treatment.
claims.source_text: A reduction of ≥ 50% in MPN‐SAF TSS is widely accepted as a clinically meaningful treatment response, according to consensus from the International Working Group for Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Research and Treatment (IWG‐MRT). … Importantly, the guidelines stress the practical implementation of symptom assessment at every clinical encounter, both to track disease evolution and to evaluate therapeutic efficacy. Symptom progression, even in the absence of overt hematologic progression, is now regarded as a sufficient indication for therapeutic escalation or modification.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk-score with molecular models:** MIPSS70+ v2.0 (MIPSSv2) for primary MF and MYSEC-PM for MF secondary to PV/ET. Observe or treat symptoms in low-risk disease; consider high- and very-high-risk patients early for allogeneic stem cell transplant.
claims.source_text: MIPSS70+ v2.0 (MIPSSv2) is recommended as the preferred model for primary MF, combining clinical variables with high‐risk mutations and cytogenetics to stratify patients into five risk categories with defined survival estimates. For secondary MF, MYSEC‐PM provides a validated alternative. Both scores allow dynamic reassessment and are easily applied in clinical practice via online tools. These models directly inform management: low‐risk patients are typically observed or treated symptomatically, whereas high‐ and very‐high‐risk patients should be considered early for allogeneic stem cell transplantation
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do NGS and conventional cytogenetics at baseline and during follow-up**, especially if transplant-eligible. FISH does not replace karyotyping for prognostic scoring.
claims.source_text: The guideline also stresses the importance of comprehensive NGS and cytogenetic testing at baseline and during follow‐up, particularly in transplant‐eligible individuals, to refine risk stratification and to anticipate progression and clonal evolution … It also explicitly notes that FISH is not a substitute for conventional karyotyping in prognostic scoring, particularly for MIPSSv2.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnosis combines marrow histology** (hypercellularity, atypical megakaryopoiesis, reticulin fibrosis grade 0–1) with a JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation or another clonal marker, plus minor criteria such as anaemia, leukocytosis, splenomegaly or a raised LDH. The clinician and an expert haematopathologist should discuss the case.
claims.source_text: Diagnosis requires integration of bone marrow histopathology-characterized by hypercellularity, atypical megakaryopoiesis, and minimal reticulin fibrosis (grade 0-1)-with molecular findings (JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutations, or other clonal markers) and minor criteria including anemia, leukocytosis, splenomegaly, or elevated LDH. Communication between clinicians and expert hematopathologists is strongly recommended to ensure diagnostic precision.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pre-PMF has a worse prognosis than ET**, with more progression to overt MF, more secondary AML and shorter survival.
claims.source_text: Importantly, patients with pre‐PMF have a worse prognosis than ET, with higher rates of progression to overt MF, secondary acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and inferior overall survival.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat by risk.** Observe low-risk, asymptomatic patients with low-dose aspirin. Use hydroxyurea or interferon-alpha for symptoms, high counts or thrombotic risk. Ropeginterferon-alpha is emerging as the preferred disease-modifying option in younger patients.
claims.source_text: Low‐risk, asymptomatic patients can often be managed with observation and low‐dose aspirin to reduce thrombotic events. Cytoreductive therapy with hydroxyurea or interferon‐alpha is indicated in symptomatic patients, or in those with high counts or thrombotic risk. Interferon, particularly ropeginterferon‐alpha, is emerging as a preferred disease‐modifying therapy in younger patients with long life expectancy, supported by early data suggesting reduction in JAK2 allele burden and potential delay of disease progression.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Thrombosis in PMF:** anticoagulation is the backbone for venous thrombosis, including at atypical sites. Antiplatelet therapy is mainly for selected arterial or microvascular events. Cytopenias, splenomegaly, portal hypertension and bleeding risk mean each case needs individual judgement.
claims.source_text: Management of thrombotic events in PMF should be individualized according to thrombotic site, bleeding risk, platelet count, and concomitant cytopenias. In general, anticoagulation is the backbone of therapy for venous thromboembolism, including thrombosis at atypical sites, whereas antiplatelet therapy may be considered mainly in selected arterial or microvascular manifestations. In contrast to ET or PV, thrombotic management in PMF is more frequently complicated by anemia, thrombocytopenia, advanced splenomegaly, portal hypertension, and an increased bleeding risk; therefore, treatment decisions require careful case‐by‐case evaluation.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **JAK inhibitors are standard care for symptomatic MF.** Ruxolitinib stays first-line for most patients, with evidence for better symptom control and overall survival.
claims.source_text: designates JAK inhibitors as the standard of care for symptomatic MF, targeting splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms. Ruxolitinib remains the first‐line agent for the majority of patients, supported by extensive evidence demonstrating improvements in symptom control and overall survival.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Choose by clinical profile:** ruxolitinib for classic symptomatic disease with splenomegaly, fedratinib after ruxolitinib failure, and momelotinib when anaemia is present.
claims.source_text: Therapeutic choice should therefore be stratified according to the patient's clinical profile: ruxolitinib for classic symptomatic disease with splenomegaly, fedratinib for ruxolitinib failure, and momelotinib in the presence of anemia.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fedratinib is mainly second-line**, but it can be a first-line alternative when ruxolitinib is contraindicated or with comorbidities such as non-melanoma skin cancer, lymphoproliferative disorders or thrombocytopenia.
claims.source_text: Although fedratinib is approved for use in the front‐line setting, ONKOPEDIA positions it primarily as a second‐line option, reflecting clinical practice patterns and comparative experience. However, it may be considered as a first‐line alternative in selected patients, such as those with contraindications to ruxolitinib or specific comorbidities, such as non‐melanoma skin cancer, lymphoproliferative disorders, or thrombocytopenia.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Dose ruxolitinib by the approved platelet-based label.** Take care with marked baseline anaemia but avoid systematic underdosing. With clinically relevant anaemia, momelotinib may be the better first-line JAK inhibitor.
claims.source_text: Initial dosing of ruxolitinib should primarily follow the approved platelet‐based prescribing information. In patients with marked baseline anemia, caution is warranted, but systematic underdosing should be avoided; in appropriate patients with clinically relevant anemia, momelotinib may represent a preferable first‐line JAK inhibitor option.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Momelotinib improves anaemia and reduces transfusion dependence**, unlike other JAK inhibitors. Its long-term efficacy and survival compared with ruxolitinib or fedratinib are still uncertain.
claims.source_text: Unlike other JAK inhibitors, momelotinib improves anemia outcomes, reducing transfusion dependence, which is of particular relevance in advanced disease stages … Although momelotinib offers clinically meaningful benefits in anemia control, uncertainties remain regarding its long‐term comparative efficacy and survival benefit relative to ruxolitinib or fedratinib, particularly outside the context of clinical trials.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Add-on anaemia strategies (ESAs, luspatercept with a JAK inhibitor) rest mostly on early-phase or non-randomised data.** Randomised comparative evidence is lacking.
claims.source_text: It should be noted that many combination approaches, including JAK inhibitor-based combinations with ESAs or luspatercept, are supported predominantly by early‐phase or non‐randomized studies. Robust comparative data from randomized trials are still lacking.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **JAK inhibitors are not curative.** Their gains in symptoms, performance status and spleen size also make them a bridge to transplant in eligible patients.
claims.source_text: JAK inhibitors are not curative, but their capacity to improve symptom burden, performance status, and splenomegaly is crucial not only for long‐term palliation but also as a bridge to transplantation in eligible patients.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second line in Germany is fedratinib or momelotinib only.** A German regulatory statement deems all other combinations off-label, which excludes pacritinib. NCCN instead prefers pacritinib for higher-risk MF with platelets < 50 × 10^9/L when transplant is not feasible.
claims.source_text: For higher‐risk MF with platelets ≥ 50 × 10^9/L, ruxolitinib or fedratinib are category 1 options; if platelets < 50 × 10^9/L and transplant is not feasible, pacritinib is a category 1 preferred regimen … directs second‐line JAK inhibition after ruxolitinib to a binary decision between fedratinib and momelotinib, with "all other combinations deemed off‐label"-implicitly excluding pacritinib from routine use in Germany.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Check the RR6 score at 6 months on ruxolitinib.** Its inputs are a ruxolitinib dose < 20 mg bid, a palpable spleen reduction of ≤ 30% at 3 and 6 months, and red-cell transfusion need. RR6 high risk should prompt a switch of JAK inhibitor, a clinical trial or fast-tracked transplant evaluation.
claims.source_text: The German text details the RR6 inputs (ruxolitinib dose < 20 mg bid, ≤ 30% palpable spleen reduction at 3/6 months, and red‐cell transfusion need) and stratifies 6‐month outcomes into low/intermediate/high risk to trigger timely second‐line switch and transplant planning. … The guideline therefore recommends early identification of RR6 high‐risk patients to prompt timely therapeutic adaptations, including switching to an alternative JAK inhibitor, referral for clinical trial participation, or expedited evaluation for allogeneic transplantation in eligible individuals.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Read RR6 in context:** it depends on spleen measurement and can misclassify slow responders, so interpret it alongside longitudinal clinical assessment.
claims.source_text: Its reliance on spleen volume measurements may restrict applicability in settings where standardized imaging is not routinely available, and it may misclassify patients with delayed but ultimately meaningful responses. Therefore, RR6 should be interpreted in the context of longitudinal clinical assessment.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Allogeneic transplant is the only curative option; refer early.** ONKOPEDIA follows the 2023 EBMT/ELN recommendations, considering biological age up to about 75 years. Transplant-eligible patients on a JAK inhibitor need an RR6 evaluation at 6 months, and a high-risk score means immediate transplant evaluation.
claims.source_text: Despite these advances, the guidelines reaffirm that allogeneic stem cell transplantation remains the only curative option. … ONKOPEDIA adopts the 2023 EBMT/ELN recommendations more directly, advocating early transplant referral and incorporating biological age considerations up to approximately 75 years. The German guideline specifically mandates that transplant‐eligible patients receiving JAK inhibitors undergo RR6‐based evaluation after 6 months, with high‐risk scores prompting immediate transplant evaluation.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give a JAK inhibitor before transplant** when the spleen is ≥ 5 cm or causing symptoms.
claims.source_text: Additionally, ONKOPEDIA emphasizes that patients with splenomegaly ≥ 5 cm or splenomegaly‐related symptoms should receive JAK inhibitor therapy prior to transplant
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Splenic irradiation or splenectomy for marked splenomegaly is an individual decision.** Irradiation is less invasive and can bridge to transplant. Splenectomy reduces spleen burden more but carries considerable perioperative morbidity and mortality.
claims.source_text: Splenic irradiation may be considered as a bridge to transplantation and is generally less invasive, whereas splenectomy may offer a more substantial reduction of splenic burden in selected cases but is associated with considerable perioperative morbidity and mortality.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer clinical trial enrolment whenever possible.**
claims.source_text: Patients should be considered for clinical trial enrollment whenever possible, both to access these novel agents and to contribute to the rapidly expanding body of evidence guiding future practice.
claims.locator: DGHO MPN expert panel (Griesshammer M, Al-Ali HK, Baerlocher GM, et al.), International Journal of Cancer (Wiley/UICC), 'The German ONKOPEDIA Guideline for Myelofibrosis in 2025 — Recommendations of an MPN Expert Panel of the German Society for Hematology and Oncology (DGHO)', published 21 June 2026, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13432566/, retrieved 2026-09-23
